info.title: GlassFrog API v5 (Beta)
info.description:
The GlassFrog API v5 provides programmatic access to your organization's
Holacracy structure — roles, accountabilities, domains, assignments, and more.

> **⚠️ Beta Notice:** This API is in beta. Breaking changes may occur.
> See the **Release Notes** section at the end of this document for updates.

## Authentication

All requests require a credential: an API v5 key, or an OAuth 2.0 access
token obtained through the authorization-code flow. Send an API key in
either the `X-Auth-Token` header or the `Authorization` header as a Bearer
credential — the two are equivalent. API v5 keys are distinct from v3 keys
and must be generated separately.

```
X-Auth-Token: your_v5_api_key_here
```
```
Authorization: Bearer your_v5_api_key_here
```
```
Authorization: Bearer gfo_your_oauth_access_token
```

OAuth access tokens start with `gfo_`, expire after 30 minutes and are
renewed with the `gfr_`-prefixed refresh token at `/oauth/token`. They are
accepted only in the `Authorization: Bearer` header — an OAuth token in
`X-Auth-Token` is rejected. A refresh token is never a valid bearer
credential.

Third-party clients, MCP clients included, get these tokens through the
OAuth 2.0 sign-in flow described in the OAuth 2.0 guide at
`/api/v5/docs/oauth`. API keys keep working alongside it.

If both headers are sent, `X-Auth-Token` takes precedence; an invalid
credential in either header is rejected rather than falling back to the
other header or credential kind.

Each credential is scoped to a single organization and person and carries
the grant set chosen when it was issued; permissions follow the caller's
membership in that organization, narrowed to those grants.

### OAuth 2.0 discovery and client registration

GlassFrog's authorization server lives at the root of the host that serves
the API, outside `/api/v5`. Clients discover it rather than hard-coding it:

- `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC 9728), also served at
  `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/v5/mcp`, describes the MCP
  endpoint and names the authorization server. The core-tools MCP endpoint,
  `/api/v5/mcp/core`, has its own document at
  `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/v5/mcp/core`; a token works on
  both. Unauthenticated `401` responses point here through the
  `resource_metadata` parameter of their `WWW-Authenticate` challenge.
- `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414) lists the
  authorization (`/oauth/authorize`), token (`/oauth/token`), revocation
  (`/oauth/revoke`) and registration (`/oauth/register`) endpoints. The
  flow is the authorization-code grant with PKCE (`S256` only) and refresh
  tokens; the only scope is `api`.
- `POST /oauth/register` (RFC 7591) registers a client. Every registered
  client is public: it gets a `client_id`, no secret, and authenticates at
  the token endpoint with PKCE alone (`token_endpoint_auth_method: none`).

```
POST /oauth/register
Content-Type: application/json

{"client_name": "Example Client",
 "redirect_uris": ["https://client.example.com/oauth/callback"]}
```
```
HTTP/1.1 201 Created

{"client_id": "example-client-id", "client_id_issued_at": 1790000000,
 "client_name": "Example Client",
 "redirect_uris": ["https://client.example.com/oauth/callback"],
 "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none",
 "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
 "response_types": ["code"], "scope": "api"}
```

Redirect URIs must be absolute `https` URIs without a fragment or user
information, and must not point at a loopback, private or link-local host;
custom schemes and `urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob` are refused. The exception is
a native app's loopback redirect (RFC 8252): plain `http` to `127.0.0.1`,
`[::1]` or `localhost`. A client may register up to five, and the one sent
at authorization must match one of them exactly, except that a loopback
redirect's port may differ. `client_name` is optional, at most 100 characters, and may not
contain markup or control characters; the consent screen shows it as
reported by the client, next to the redirect host. A refused registration
answers `400` with an RFC 7591 error body, `{"error": "invalid_redirect_uri"
| "invalid_client_metadata", "error_description": "..."}`. Registration is
rate-limited per client address; a client that nobody authorizes within 14
days is deleted.

## Pagination

List endpoints use cursor-based pagination. Use `per_page` and `cursor` to
page through results. Pass `cursor` the `next_cursor` value from the
previous response.

Page size limits belong to the endpoint, not to the API as a whole. Most
endpoints default to 100 records per page and allow at most 500. Three goal
and target sub-resource endpoints default to 25 and allow at most 500:
`GET /goals/{goal_id}/targets`, `GET /goals/{goal_id}/progress`, and
`GET /targets/{target_id}/progress`. All other goal and target endpoints
default to 100. `GET /search` defaults to 25 and allows at most 100. Read
`meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see the size the server
applied.

Values above an endpoint's maximum return `400 Bad Request` with a `message`
explaining the limit — callers should not assume the server silently clamped.

A blank, zero, negative, or non-numeric `per_page` is not rejected. It falls
back to a fixed size. That size is not always the endpoint's own default:

- Most endpoints fall back to 100. That is also their default.
- The three goal and target sub-resource endpoints above fall back to 100, but their default is 25.
- `GET /search` falls back to 25. That is also its default.

```json
{
  "data": [...],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "per_page": 100,
      "has_next_page": true,
      "next_cursor": "role_abc123..."
    }
  }
}
```

### Result order

List endpoints return records in the order the server stored them. The
oldest stored record comes first. New records are added at the end. This
order is stable.

These endpoints page by record id. The cursor is exclusive: a page starts
after the last record of the page before it. While the cursor names a
record that still exists, paging returns each record once — it never skips
a record and never repeats one. If that record has been deleted, the
endpoint returns the first page again.

Storage order is not the same as the `created_at` field. Some records were
given a `created_at` value after they were stored, so the two can differ.
Sort the records yourself if you need them in `created_at` order.

`GET /search` is the other exception. It ranks results by relevance, not by id.
Its paging has a known defect. It is not fixed yet.

The record at a page boundary can be returned again on the next page, so
dedupe by `id` as you page. A page walk is also not guaranteed to return
every result: in a sample of four queries, two returned fewer records than
the same query returned in one page. Do not treat a finished `/search` page
walk as a complete result set.

## Unrecognised query parameters

The API ignores query parameters it does not recognise. It does not reject
them. A misspelled or wrong parameter name is dropped, and the request
still succeeds. You get no error and no warning.

This matters most for pagination. Send the cursor under a name the endpoint
does not read, and the API returns the first page again, with
`has_next_page` still `true`. Two failures follow:

- A loop that pages until `has_next_page` is `false` never ends.
- A caller that reads one page believes it read the whole collection. It
  sees only the records on the first page. The rest are never returned.

To confirm you are paging, check that each page returns different ids.

## Includes

Detail endpoints support `?include=` to embed related resources.
Pass a comma-separated list of valid include names.

## Legacy IDs (transition-only)

> **⚠️ Temporary migration bridge — will be removed.** The `legacy_id`
> field described here exists solely to ease the v3→v5 transition and
> **retires when the v3 API retires.** Do not build durable integrations on
> it; use the v5 TypeID (`id`) as the stable identifier.

v5 identifies resources by opaque TypeIDs (e.g. `org_1a2b…`, `role_9f8e…`),
which intentionally differ from the v3 sequential numeric IDs (e.g. the org
id `38655` shown in the web UI). To help integrators migrating from v3
correlate the two, pass `?include_legacy_id=true` on any standard resource
endpoint (and `/me`). Each resource in the response then carries an extra
`legacy_id` field holding its v3 sequential integer id:

```
GET /api/v5/me?include_legacy_id=true
→ { "data": { "organization": { "id": "org_1a2b…", "legacy_id": 38655, … } } }
```

Notes:
- **Opt-in and off by default** — `legacy_id` is omitted unless the param is
  passed, keeping the default v5 contract free of v3 coupling.
- **Actors backed by agents return `null`** — agents have no v3 representation.
- Applies to the standard resource list/show endpoints and `/me`. Nested
  `?include=` embeds and the cross-model `search` / agent-`context`
  aggregation endpoints do not carry `legacy_id`.

## Optimistic Concurrency (ETags)

GET responses for mutable resources include an `ETag` header — a hash of the
resource's current state. To prevent stale writes, send the ETag back on
PUT/PATCH via the `If-Match` header:

```
GET /api/v5/notes/rnot_abc123
→ ETag: "a1b2c3..."

PATCH /api/v5/notes/rnot_abc123
If-Match: "a1b2c3..."
→ 200 OK          (ETag matched — write accepted)
→ 409 Conflict     (resource changed since your read — re-fetch and retry)
```

If `If-Match` is omitted, the update proceeds unconditionally (last-write-wins).
This keeps it simple for consumers who don't need concurrency protection.

## Errors

Errors follow the RFC 9457 Problem Details shape (the backward-compatible
2023 successor to RFC 7807) and are served with
`Content-Type: application/problem+json`:

```json
{
  "type": "about:blank",
  "title": "Not Found",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "Not Found"
}
```

`type`, `title`, `status`, and `detail` are always present. Additional
members ("extensions" in RFC 9457 terms) may appear alongside them.

## Rate Limiting

API requests are rate-limited per organization on a rolling 1-hour window.
Limits depend on your plan:

| Plan | Limit |
|------|-------|
| Free / Restricted | 50 requests / hour |
| Premium | `member_count × 500` requests / hour |

Every response includes rate limit headers:

| Header | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Maximum requests allowed in the current window |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests remaining in the current window |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix epoch timestamp when the window resets |

When the limit is exceeded, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a
`Retry-After` header and an RFC 9457 Problem Details body:

```json
{
  "type": "about:blank",
  "title": "Too Many Requests",
  "status": 429,
  "detail": "Rate limit exceeded. Try again in 42 seconds."
}
```

## Release Notes

Curated highlights of notable changes and clarifications. This section is the
canonical changelog for API v5 — check here for updates.

### Beta (current)

- **Starting a session again is safe.** `POST /agents/{agent_id}/sessions`
  in a scope that already has an open session returns that session and its
  full context with `200`, instead of `409`. Call it whenever the role
  context has dropped out of your window. `409` now means only that both
  calls carry an `identifier` and they differ.
- **One feed for every channel.** `GET /me/messages` lists messages across
  all of the caller's channels, oldest first, with the same `unread`,
  `role` and `since` filters. Its `next_cursor` is returned whenever there
  is a position to resume from (absent only on an empty page with no
  `cursor`), so a sync client can store it and resume without gaps or
  duplicates.
  `POST /me/messages/read` and `POST /channels/{id}/read` with `up_to`
  mark read up to a message rather than up to now.
- **Native apps can register a loopback redirect.** Client registration
  accepts `http://127.0.0.1`, `http://[::1]` and `http://localhost`
  redirect URIs, and authorization ignores their port, so CLI and desktop
  clients (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code) can sign in with OAuth.
- **Read only new channel messages.** `GET /channels/{channel_id}/messages`
  takes `unread=true` (after the caller's read watermark, optionally a
  role's), `since` (after a given time) and `order=desc` (newest first).
  Without them, responses are unchanged.
- **Projects and actions carry `actor_id`.** Each project and action names
  the person (`per_`) or agent (`agt_`) on it (the filler whose focus it is,
  or the owner of an individual initiative), and the project and action
  lists take `?actor_id=` to keep one actor's items, so co-fillers of a role
  can be told apart. `GET /me/projects?individual_initiative=true`
  lists your individual initiative projects.
- **Email changes are confirmed before they apply.** `PATCH /actors/{id}`
  with a new `email` for a person whose address is confirmed returns 200,
  but `email` keeps its old value until the person follows the
  confirmation link sent to the new address.
- **Focus & election data comes via `?include=assignments`.** A node's
  assignments — carrying focus and election data — are embedded by requesting
  `GET /roles/{id}/tree?include=assignments`. Note that `?include=members`
  returns bare fillers *without* focus or election data; use
  `?include=assignments` when you need focus.
- **Assignments API surface.** Assignments are accessed through the nested
  collection paths `GET`/`POST /roles/{id}/assignments` and
  `GET /actors/{id}/assignments`, plus `PATCH`/`DELETE /assignments/{id}` for
  a single assignment. There is no standalone `GET /assignments` collection
  endpoint — the tree's `?include=assignments` already returns every focus in
  one call.
- **`ElectRoleFiller` term is `elected_until`.** Set the election term on an
  `ElectRoleFiller` proposal change with `elected_until` (a `YYYY-MM-DD`
  date), the same name assignments use. The undocumented `assignedUntil`
  key is now rejected with a 422.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of roles in the organization. Each role includes
its accountabilities, domains, fillers, and flags inline. Use filters to
narrow results by parent role or assigned person.

parameters.name: parent_role_id
parameters.description: Filter to roles within a specific parent role.

parameters.name: person_id
parameters.description: Filter to roles assigned to a specific person.

parameters.name: has_subroles
parameters.description:
Filter by whether a role has sub-roles. `true` returns only roles
with sub-roles; `false` returns only leaf roles. Omit to
return all roles.

get.description:
Returns a single role by its ID. Use `?include=` to embed related
resources such as assignments, sub-roles, parent role, policies, or notes.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to include.

get.description:
Returns the immediate child roles of a role (its subroles).
For leaf roles with no subroles, returns an empty array.

Navigate the org hierarchy by walking this tree:
```
GET /roles                          → top-level roles
GET /roles/:id/subroles            → what's inside this role
GET /roles/:id/subroles?include=subroles  → two levels deep
```

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to include on each sub-role.

200.description: A paginated list of child roles.

get.summary: List actors filling a role's subroles
get.description:
Returns actors (humans and agents) filling any direct sub-role of this
role. One level of nesting. Cross-linked assignments are excluded.

Only available on expanded roles (where `has_subroles` is `true`).
Leaf roles return 404. Same response shape as `GET /actors`.

Use `?kind=human` to filter to human actors only, or use the
`/roles/{id}/subroles/people` alias.

200.description: A paginated list of subrole actors.

get.summary: List people filling a role's subroles
get.description:
Alias for `GET /roles/{id}/subroles/actors?kind=human`. Returns only
human actors (people) filling any direct sub-role of this role.

Only available on expanded roles (where `has_subroles` is `true`).
Leaf roles return 404. Same response shape as `GET /actors`.

200.description: A paginated list of people filling subroles.

get.summary: List projects rolled up across a role's subroles
get.description:
Returns projects owned by any direct sub-role of this role. Same
response shape as `GET /roles/:id/projects`. One level of nesting.

Only available on expanded roles (where `has_subroles` is `true`).
Leaf roles return 404.

get.summary: List actions rolled up across a role's subroles
get.description:
Returns actions owned by any direct sub-role of this role. Same
response shape as `GET /roles/:id/actions`. One level of nesting.

Only available on expanded roles (where `has_subroles` is `true`).
Leaf roles return 404.

Use `?individual_initiative=true` to list individual initiative actions
across subrole circles instead of role-owned actions.

parameters.name: individual_initiative
parameters.description: When `true`, returns individual initiative actions for sub-role circles instead of role-owned actions. Omit or pass `false` for the default behavior.

get.summary: List policies rolled up across a role's subroles
get.description:
Returns policies attached to any direct sub-role of this role. Same
response shape as `GET /roles/:id/policies`. One level of nesting.

Only available on expanded roles (where `has_subroles` is `true`).
Leaf roles return 404.

get.summary: Get the full subtree rooted at a role
get.description:
Returns the complete role hierarchy below (and including) the
requested root role, as a single nested tree node. Useful for org-chart
rendering and for agents orienting to a branch of the organization in
one call.

The per-node shape is "light" by default (id, name, purpose,
parent_role_id, has_subroles, flags, children). Use `?include=` to
add `accountabilities`, `domains`, `members` (fillers), and/or
`assignments` (with focus and election data) to every node.
Policies, notes, and skills — which are often large —
are not offered as tree-level includes; fetch them via `/roles/{id}`
for a specific role.

**Recursion is intentional** and the whole point of this endpoint,
in contrast to `/roles/{id}/subroles` which returns only direct
children.

**Pagination:** not supported. GlassFrog organizations are small
enough (typically 100–500 roles) that returning the full tree in one
response is the simpler and more useful design. Use `?depth=` when
you need to bound response size.

**Caching:** responses carry an `ETag` header whose fingerprint
combines the maximum `updated_at` across the subtree with the
requester's authorization digest. Send `If-None-Match` on subsequent
requests to receive a `304 Not Modified` when nothing visible has
changed.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description:
Maximum depth of descendants to return. `0` returns the root
node alone with no children; `1` returns the root plus its
direct children; and so on. Omit for the full subtree.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of extra per-node fields. Unknown values are
silently ignored.

200.description: The full subtree rooted at the requested role.

304.description: Not Modified. The client's `If-None-Match` matches the current fingerprint.

get.description:
Convenience alias for `GET /roles/{id}/tree` with the requester's
organization's anchor role as the root — i.e., "the whole org". All
query parameters and response semantics match `/roles/{id}/tree`.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description:
Maximum depth of descendants to return. `0` returns the root
node alone; `1` returns root plus direct children; and so on.
Omit for the full subtree.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of extra per-node fields to include on
each tree node: `accountabilities`, `domains`, `members`,
`assignments`.

200.description: The full org tree rooted at the anchor role.

304.description: Not Modified. The client's `If-None-Match` matches the current fingerprint.

get.description:
Returns everything an agent (or person) needs to fill a role — structured
organizational context in a single API call. The response is a hypermedia
document: full content for critical items (identity, role definition, skills),
indexes with API links for everything else (policies, notes, projects).

**Progressive disclosure:** Indexed items include a `url` field pointing to
the full-detail API endpoint. Call those endpoints for complete content.

**Agent identity:** The `agent` section is only present when the API key
belongs to an agent-kind actor. Human actors receive all other sections.

parameters.name: include_skills
parameters.description: When true, inline every linked skill's body in the response regardless of the per-link `load_at_boot` flag. Default: false (only boot-loaded skills are inlined).

200.description: The full context for filling this role.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of actors (humans and agents) in the organization.
Use `?kind=` to filter by type. The `/people` and `/agents` aliases apply
the kind filter automatically.

parameters.name: role_id
parameters.description: Filter to actors filling a specific role.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Filter by exact email address (case-insensitive). Returns actors matching the given email within the caller's organization.

post.summary: Invite a person to the organization
post.description:
Creates a new person and membership in the organization (or adds an existing
person by email). Sends an invitation email. Requires org admin.

get.description:
Returns a single actor by ID. Accepts both `per_` (human) and `agt_` (agent)
prefixed IDs. Use `?include=` to embed roles or assignments.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The actor's unique identifier (per_ or agt_ prefix).

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to include.

patch.description:
Updates a person's name, email, or admin status. Org admins can update
any member; non-admins can only update themselves.

An email change on a person whose current address is confirmed does not
take effect immediately: a confirmation link is sent to the new address,
and `email` keeps its old value until that link is followed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The actor's unique identifier (per_ or agt_ prefix).

delete.summary: Remove a person from the organization
delete.description:
Removes the person's membership in the organization, along with all
role assignments, unaccepted proposals, and taggings. The person record
itself is deactivated if they have no remaining memberships.
Requires org admin.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The actor's unique identifier (per_ or agt_ prefix).

get.description:
Returns the authenticated actor's own record, bundled with organization
and membership. This is typically the first call an API consumer makes
to orient itself.

Use `?include=roles` to embed the roles the requester fills in the
response — saving the follow-up call to `/me/roles` when a client
needs both identity and role context.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to embed.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of roles the requester fills via a primary,
non-discarded assignment. Same response shape as `GET /roles`.

200.description: A paginated list of the requester's roles.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of projects owned by roles the requester
fills (primary assignments). Use `?status=` to filter.
Use `?individual_initiative=true` to list the requester's individual
initiative projects instead of role-owned projects.
Use `?actor_id=` to keep only one actor's projects, e.g. your own on
a role you share with other fillers.

parameters.name: individual_initiative
parameters.description: When `true`, returns the requester's individual initiative projects instead of role-owned projects. Omit or pass `false` for the default behavior (role-owned projects only). Any other value returns 422.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of actions owned by roles the requester
fills (primary assignments). Use `?status=` to filter.
Use `?individual_initiative=true` to list the requester's individual
initiative actions instead of role-owned actions.
Use `?actor_id=` to keep only one actor's actions, e.g. your own on
a role you share with other fillers.

parameters.name: individual_initiative
parameters.description: When `true`, returns the requester's individual initiative actions instead of role-owned actions. Omit or pass `false` for the default behavior (role-owned actions only). Any other value returns 422.

get.summary: List messages across the authenticated actor's channels
get.description:
The machine feed for sync clients: every message in every channel
the caller belongs to, oldest first, in one list. That's the channel
of each circle the caller fills a role in, plus the channels of the
caller's own leaf roles. Soft-deleted messages are omitted. Each
message carries its `channel_id`. Thread replies are included,
each with its `thread_id`, unlike on
`GET /channels/{channel_id}/messages`, which leaves them out by
default.

- `unread=true` returns, per channel, only the messages created after
  the caller's watermark on that channel (the newest one, or with
  `role` that role's). No watermark means everything is unread.
- `role` narrows the feed to that role's channels (and, with
  `unread`, its watermarks). The caller must currently fill the
  role (422 otherwise).
- `since` returns messages created strictly after a time the client
  holds. It can't be combined with `unread` (422).

Messages are ordered by `created_at`, then id. `next_cursor` is
returned whenever there is a position to resume from: the last
message on the page, or the cursor you passed if the page is empty.
It is absent only on an empty page with no `cursor`. Store it and pass it back as `cursor`
to get only messages after it, each exactly once, even when
timestamps tie. An unknown `cursor` returns 422 rather than
restarting from the beginning. Advance watermarks with
`POST /me/messages/read` or `POST /channels/{id}/read`, each with
`up_to`.

The feed includes the caller's own messages. A circle channel's
messages appear in the `role` feed of every role the caller fills
in that circle, so a client polling per role should dedupe by id.
`created_at` is assigned when the message is written, so a write
that commits late can, rarely, land behind a cursor or watermark
already handed out. Watermarks compare `created_at` alone, so
marking read up to a message also marks read any message with the
identical `created_at` (to the microsecond), delivered or not.

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description:
When `true`, return only messages created after the caller's
watermark on each channel.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description:
Only this role's channels, using its watermarks with `unread`.
The caller must currently fill the role (422 otherwise). Unlike
on `GET /channels/{channel_id}/messages`, `role` works without
`unread`: here it also selects channels.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Return only messages created strictly after this time.

post.summary: Mark the message feed read up to a message
post.description:
Advances the caller's watermark on every channel of
`GET /me/messages` (narrowed by `role`) to `up_to`'s `created_at`.
Watermarks never rewind. Pass the last message you processed, so
anything posted after your read stays unread.

Without `role` the person-level watermarks advance on every channel
of the feed, including channels the client didn't process. A client
that delivers per role or per channel should mark read with `role`,
or with `POST /channels/{id}/read` and `up_to`. With `role`, that
role's watermarks advance on its channels only. Channels the caller's credential can't write to are
skipped. The response lists only the channels whose watermark
moved.

up_to.description: The message to mark read up to, from any channel.

role.description: Only this role's channels and watermarks. The caller must fill it.

get.description:
Self-context for the authenticated caller, in one call: the full list of
roles the caller fills, and — with `?role=role_xxx` — that role's
definition and governance context.

Serves any authenticated caller. The agent-identity section (name,
description, SOUL-style context blob, configuration) and agent-level
skills (by ID — fetch full content via `/skills/{id}`) are present

**Content size limit.** `content` has a maximum size in characters.

because an agent reads a skill in a single response, and an oversized
skill cannot be delivered. The 422 body names the submitted size, the

patch.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Updates the name and/or content of an
existing skill.

**Ownership.** Update requires the caller to be a linked owner of the
skill: an agent it is linked to, a filler of a role it is linked to,
or the operator of a linked agent. An orphan skill (`ownership:
orphan`, zero kept links) may be updated by any org member. Org admins
may always update. A denial carries a `reason` member: `ownership_required`,
or `ai_integration_disabled` when the org flag is off.

Supports optimistic concurrency via `If-Match`. When present, the
update only proceeds if the ETag matches the current resource state.
Omit `If-Match` for unconditional (last-write-wins) updates.

**Content size limit.** `content` has a maximum size in characters.
Content over the limit returns 422 and is not saved. The 422 body names
the submitted size, the limit, and the configuration key that set the
limit, in the `content_length`, `max_content_length`, and
`limit_config_key` members. Split the skill into smaller skills to save
it.

delete.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Soft-deletes a skill. The skill is no

**Ownership.** Delete requires SOLE ownership: the caller (or the
agent it operates) must be the skill's only linked actor
(`ownership: sole`). A co-owned skill (2+ kept links) cannot be
deleted by any linked actor — unlink your own side instead, which
promotes the remaining actor to sole owner. An orphan skill may be
deleted by any org member. Org admins may always delete, including
co-owned skills. A denial carries a `reason` member:
`sole_ownership_required` (co-owned), `ownership_required` (not a
linked owner), or `ai_integration_disabled`.

post.summary: Create a governance proposal (draft)
post.description:
**Premium — requires async proposals.** Creates a proposal in `draft`
state, anchored to an existing tension. Each entry in `changes` is a
governance command (create role, add accountability, etc.) applied
atomically at acceptance time. Returns 403 when async proposals are
not enabled.

Advancing the proposal to circulation happens via a separate action
call: `POST /proposals/{id}/propose`.

get.description:
Returns a proposal with its changes, response summary stats, and the
list of transitions the caller may invoke on it right now
(`available_transitions`). Per-person response attribution is
intentionally not exposed.

post.summary: Advance a draft proposal into circulation
post.description:
**Premium — requires async proposals.** Advances a `draft` proposal
to `proposed_outside_meeting` (the shortcut-path circulation state)
and auto-registers the proposer's implicit `no_objection` response.
Returns 403 when async proposals are not enabled.

The backend dispatches `propose` to the appropriate internal path
(shortcut / meeting-queue / CL-forward / etc.) based on circle + org
config. Today only the shortcut path exists; future config-driven
paths will share this same API surface (callers don't choose the path
— the org's config does).

Allowed when the caller appears in `available_transitions` for this
proposal — typically the proposer of a `draft` proposal.

Implications:
  * Notifications fire (per the existing
    `Notifications::NotifyNewAsyncProposal` chain — Slack /
    email / etc., depending on the circle's notifications config).
  * `response_deadline` is set from the circle's
    `proposal_auto_accept_day_limit`.
  * Proposer's implicit `no_objection` is recorded, but is **excluded**
    from `received_response_count` (which counts only *expected*
    responders) — the proposer's own consent can never satisfy the
    auto-accept quota.

post.summary: Withdraw a circulating proposal back to draft
post.description:
**Premium — requires async proposals.** Returns a
`proposed_outside_meeting` or `escalated` proposal to `draft`.
Allowed for the proposer (and admins) when the proposal appears in
`available_transitions`. Returns 403 when async proposals are not
enabled.

Implications:
  * All existing `proposal_responses` are deleted (responders will
    need to re-respond if the proposal is later re-proposed).
  * `proposed_at` and `response_deadline` are cleared.
  * The proposal can be re-edited and re-proposed.

post.summary: Add a change to a proposal
post.description:
**Premium — requires async proposals.** Appends one governance change
to the proposal and returns the whole proposal, including `valid` and
`validation_alerts`, so the caller sees the effect at once. Returns
403 when async proposals are not enabled. A change referencing a
record that doesn't exist returns 422.

patch.summary: Replace a change on a proposal
patch.description:
**Premium — requires async proposals.** Replaces the change's
command with the one given and returns the whole proposal with
validation state. The change keeps its `id`. A numeric or otherwise
malformed `id` returns 422; an unknown one returns 404.

delete.summary: Remove a change from a proposal
delete.description:
**Premium — requires async proposals.** Removes the change and
returns the whole proposal with validation state. A numeric or
otherwise malformed `id` returns 422; an unknown one returns 404.

post.summary: Record a circle member's response to a proposal
post.description:
**Premium — requires async proposals.** Returns 403 when async
proposals are not enabled.

Circle members post one of two values during the consent window:

* `no_objection` — willing to let the proposal pass as written. When
  every expected responder has `no_objection`, the cron auto-accepts.

* `bring_to_meeting` — wants to discuss the proposal in a live
  governance meeting rather than let it circulate to auto-acceptance.
  This is NOT a retracted or formally-objected-to claim; the response
  persists on the proposal and blocks auto-acceptance. When the
  circle's agenda is ready, the proposal transitions to `escalated`
  for live discussion.

One response per person per proposal (422 on second attempt).

get.description:
Returns the role's default channel, provisioning it on first fetch.
Every role has exactly one channel; post to it via
`POST /channels/{channel_id}/messages` with the returned `id`.

Returns the channels in the caller's organization. Channels are
org-open: any org member can read and post to any channel. Each
channel is a 1:1 wrapper around a Role, which defines the channel's
audience (its members, used for notifications), not an access wall:

* **Circle role** — members are the circle's role-fillers (group
  chat semantics).
* **Leaf role** — members are the role's own filler(s) (DM-like).

Membership in either case is derived dynamically from current
assignments. Channels for a circle the caller participates in
are provisioned lazily on first list/show; leaf-role channels
are provisioned lazily on direct access.

Returns a single channel by its `chn_…` id. To reach a role's
channel from the role's id, use `GET /roles/{id}/channel`.

post.summary: Mark a channel read
post.description:
Advances the caller's read watermark on the channel to now (never
rewinds), or, with `up_to`, to that message's `created_at`. Pass the
last message you read: a message posted between your read and this
call then stays unread. Unread state is computed from the caller's newest
watermark — see the `viewer_last_read_at` / `viewer_unread_count`
fields on Channel.

Optionally scope the watermark to one of the caller's roles via
`role` — multi-role actors (typically agents) can track which of
their roles have caught up. The caller must currently fill the
role (422 otherwise).

role.description: Optional role api_id to scope the watermark to.

up_to.description:
Advance to this message's `created_at` instead of now. The
message must be in this channel (422 otherwise).

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of messages in a channel, oldest stored
first by default. Use `cursor` + `per_page` for pagination.
Soft-deleted messages are omitted.

To read only what changed, filter by time:

- `unread=true` returns the messages created after the caller's read
  watermark — the one `POST /channels/{id}/read` advances. Without
  `role` that is the caller's newest watermark on the channel, the
  same one `viewer_unread_count` counts against; with `role` it is
  that role's watermark. No watermark means everything is unread.
- `since` returns the messages created strictly after a time the
  client holds itself. Message timestamps are returned to the
  second, so for gapless continuation prefer `unread` or `cursor`.

`unread` and `since` can't be combined (422).

`order=desc` returns newest first, so the last N messages is one call
with `per_page=N`. `cursor` pages onward in whichever order was
requested.

Replies inside threads are left out by default: the list holds loose
messages and each thread's root. `include_thread_messages=true`
returns every message in the channel. Read a thread through
`GET /threads/{thread_id}/messages`.

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description:
When `true`, return only messages created after the caller's read
watermark (see `POST /channels/{id}/read`).

parameters.name: role
parameters.description:
With `unread=true`, use this role's watermark instead of the
caller's newest. The caller must currently fill the role (422
otherwise); 422 without `unread=true`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Return only messages created strictly after this time.

parameters.name: include_thread_messages
parameters.description: When `true`, also return replies inside threads.

post.summary: Post a message to a channel
post.description:
Creates a new message in the channel.

Agents must post as a specific role via `from_role`. Humans may
omit `from_role` when they fill exactly one role in the channel's
circle; otherwise it must be specified.

`delivery` selects the wake class. `notify` means the message should
be announced to its recipients; `queued` means it is delivered into
the durable inbox without waking anyone, to be read at the
recipient's next natural wake. Omit it and the default is derived
from the caller — agent senders default to `queued`, human senders
to `notify`; an explicit value always wins.

`queued` is about announcement, not delivery: queued messages are
persisted, returned by the list endpoint, and counted in
`viewer_unread_count` exactly like `notify` messages.

(Server-side notification fan-out for channel messages arrives in a
follow-up release on the event substrate, and will gate recipient
delivery on `delivery`. Unread state is watermark-based — see
`POST /channels/{id}/read`.)

Replying makes a thread: give `parent` or `reply_to` pointing at a
loose message and the reply starts a thread rooted on it (or joins
that thread if it already exists). Pointing at a message already in
a thread posts into that thread. Replies stay flat under the root:
`parent_id` is always the root and `reply_to_id` keeps the direct
reply target.

get.description:
Returns the threads homed in a channel, oldest first. A thread is
one of three kinds, told apart by its fields (kind is not stored):

* **Emergent** — `anchored_to_id` and `topic` both null. Created when
  someone replies to a loose channel message; rooted on that message.
* **Work-anchored** — `anchored_to_id` set. One thread per work entity,
  globally, homed in the owning role's channel. v1 anchors: projects.
* **Topic** — `topic` set: an opaque stable name, unique per channel.

Filter by `anchored_to_id` or `topic` to find a specific thread.

parameters.name: anchored_to_id
parameters.description: Only the thread anchored to this entity.

parameters.name: topic
parameters.description: Only the thread with this topic.

post.summary: Create a thread in a channel
post.description:
Creates a work-anchored or topic thread, addressable before anyone
posts in it. Give exactly one of `anchored_to_id` or `topic`.
Emergent threads are never created here — reply to a loose message
instead.

Idempotent on the anchor or topic: when the thread already exists it
is returned with 200 (the request's `title` is ignored); a new thread
returns 201. A new thread gets a system-authored root message
(`from_person_id` null, `client` `glassfrog`) that appears in the
channel's message list.

An anchored thread must be created in its home channel, the channel
of the role that owns the anchored entity (422 otherwise). Creating it
requires being able to view the entity (404 otherwise). Person- or
circle-private projects cannot anchor a thread (403).

The author rule is the one for posting a message: an agent must pass
a `from_role` it fills, a human may omit it when unambiguous (422
otherwise, with nothing written).

get.description: Returns a single thread.

patch.description:
Gives an emergent thread an anchor or a topic. Accepted only while
both `anchored_to_id` and `topic` are null; a thread is never
re-anchored or renamed (422). Give exactly one of the two.
Uniqueness applies as on create: 422 when another thread already
holds the anchor, or the topic in this channel. An anchor must also
be homed in this thread's channel.

The author rule is the one for posting a message: an agent must pass
a `from_role` it fills, a human may omit it when unambiguous (422
otherwise, with nothing written).

get.description:
Returns the thread's messages, root first, oldest first by default.
Replies are flat under the root; `reply_to_id` carries any in-reply-to
structure. Supports the same `order` as the channel message list.

post.summary: Post a message to a thread
post.description:
Posts a reply in the thread. The message's `parent_id` is the
thread's root; `parent`, when given, must be the root. `reply_to`,
when given, must be a message in this thread. Otherwise as
`POST /channels/{channel_id}/messages`.

get.description:
Returns the project's thread: there is at most one per project,
homed in the owning role's channel. 404 until the thread exists;
`POST /projects/{project_id}/thread/messages` creates it on first
post.

post.summary: Post a message to a project's thread
post.description:
Posts to the project's thread, creating the thread first (with its
system-authored root) when it doesn't exist yet. No pre-create is
needed. Otherwise as `POST /threads/{thread_id}/messages`.

patch.description:
Edits a message body. Author-only. Sets `edited_at` so clients can
render an edited marker — messages carry no further revision
history by design.

Only `body` is applied. `delivery` is fixed at post time (the wake
decision belongs to the moment of sending) and is ignored here.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes a message. Author-only. Replies keep their threading
pointers; deleted messages are omitted from lists.

post.summary: Start an agent session
post.description:
Creates an agent session. Three modes depending on parameters:

1. `role_id` given — role session, returns role context.
2. `role_id` + `topic` — per-topic session alongside the primary.
3. Neither — agent-level session, returns agent context.

Calling it again is safe. If an active session already exists for the
same scope (agent, role, topic), it is returned unchanged with its full
context and status 200 (a new session returns 201). `identifier` is
optional; omit it if you have no stable conversation id.

Returns 403 if the agent is not assigned to the given role.
Returns 409 only when both this call and the open session carry an
`identifier` and they differ, or the open session belongs to another
organization.

parameters.name: include_skills
parameters.description: When true, inline every linked skill's body in the context response regardless of the per-link `load_at_boot` flag. Default: false (only boot-loaded skills are inlined).

parameters.name: preloaded
parameters.description: When true, skip returning context (caller already has it). Session is still registered; only the context blob is omitted.

role_id.description: Role to start a session for. Agent must be assigned.

topic.description: Topic scoping the session (e.g. ticket ID).

identifier.description: Optional client-provided session identifier. When both sides carry one and they differ, the call returns 409.

supersede.description: When true, end any existing active session for the same scope and start a fresh one instead of returning it.

200.description: An active session already existed for this scope; it is returned unchanged.

409.description: An active session exists for this scope under a different identifier, or in another organization.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of agent session records across the
organization, filtered by visibility: an agent sees only its own
sessions, a human operator sees sessions of the agents they operate,
and an org admin sees every session in the org.

Records are returned **as stored**. `status` reflects what was
recorded by the start/end lifecycle calls — nothing here checks
whether a session is really still running on its host. A record
reading `active` may correspond to a process that died without
ending its session; surfacing that disagreement is the point of the
endpoint, so the read path deliberately does not "correct" it.

`last_seen_at` is stamped by the heartbeat endpoint; sessions
that predate the feature carry a backfilled value from `updated_at`.
`liveness_state` is derived on read from `last_seen_at` and
`heartbeat_interval` — fresh, stale, ended, or unknown.
Sessions past the grace period (default 30 min) are auto-expired
by a server-side job.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Limit to sessions in this state. `active` is the reconciliation
query — it pulls just the open records. Any other value returns
`422 Unprocessable Entity`.

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: Limit to sessions belonging to this agent.

parameters.name: role_id
parameters.description: Limit to sessions started for this role.

parameters.name: topic
parameters.description: Exact match on the session's topic (e.g. a ticket id).

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description:
Exact match on the client-supplied identifier. Lets a caller that
knows its own identifier look up its own record — and so recover
its `sess_…` id — without guessing.

200.description: A paginated list of agent sessions.

get.description:
Returns a single agent session record by ID, including its summary.

The record is returned **as stored** — no liveness is computed.
Visibility follows the same rules as `listSessions`: an agent sees
its own sessions, a human operator sees sessions of the agents they
operate, and an org admin sees every session in the org.

post.summary: Send a session heartbeat
post.description:
Stamps the session's `last_seen_at` to the current time.
Used by daemons to signal process liveness — not activity-based.
Sessions past the grace period (default 30 min) are auto-expired
by a server-side job.

Accepts optional telemetry in the request body:
`context_used_pct` (context window usage percentage).

Agent-token only. The agent must own the session.

200.description: Heartbeat recorded. Returns the updated session.

post.summary: Batch heartbeat for multiple sessions
post.description:
Heartbeats multiple sessions in a single call. Designed for
supervisors that manage a fleet of sessions. Each session id
gets an individual result — ok, forbidden, or not_found.

Accepts optional per-session telemetry keyed by session id.

Agent-token only.

telemetry.description: Per-session telemetry keyed by session id.

Returns work requests visible to the caller, optionally filtered by

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Cursor for pagination (api_id of the last item on the previous page).

200.description: A paginated list of work requests.

post.summary: Create a work request
post.description: Files a role-to-role work request. The caller must fill `from_role_id`.

post.summary: Accept a work request
post.description:
Accepts a pending work request, creating the requested project or action

post.summary: Accept a work request with edits
post.description:
Accepts a pending work request after optionally modifying its description

description.description: Updated description for the work item.

note.description: Updated note for the work item.

BearerAuth.description:
Either a GlassFrog API v5 key (`Authorization: Bearer <your_v5_api_key>`,
an alias to `X-Auth-Token` for hosted clients that cannot send a custom
header) or an OAuth 2.0 access token (`Authorization: Bearer gfo_…`)
issued by GlassFrog's authorization server. The value's prefix decides
which it is; a `gfr_` refresh token is never accepted as a bearer
credential.

OAuth access tokens expire after 30 minutes and are refreshed at
`/oauth/token`; the authority they carry is the grant set the person
chose at consent. Unauthenticated responses carry an RFC 6750
`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge whose `resource_metadata` points at
the RFC 9728 protected-resource document.

Precedence: if both `X-Auth-Token` and `Authorization: Bearer` are
sent, `X-Auth-Token` is used. An invalid credential is rejected and
never falls back to the other header or credential kind.

OAuth2.description:
OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow for clients acting on a person's
behalf. Access tokens are `gfo_`-prefixed and sent as
`Authorization: Bearer gfo_…` (see BearerAuth). PKCE with `S256` is
required. The single `api` scope is a protocol formality: what limits
a token's authority is the grant set the person chose at consent, not
the scope. See the OAuth 2.0 guide at `/api/v5/docs/oauth`.

scopes.api: Call the GlassFrog API v5 within the grant set chosen at consent.

ETag.description:
Hash of the resource's current state. Pass this value back as
`If-Match` on subsequent PUT/PATCH requests to enable optimistic
concurrency checking.

RateLimitLimit.description: Maximum requests allowed in the current window.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests remaining in the current window.

RateLimitReset.description: Unix epoch timestamp when the current window resets.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (present on 429 responses).

PerPage.name: per_page
PerPage.description: Number of results per page (1–500, default 100). Values above the maximum return `400 Bad Request`; blank, zero, negative, or non-numeric values fall back to the default of 100.

PerPageGoalsAndTargets.name: per_page
PerPageGoalsAndTargets.description: Number of results per page for the goal and target endpoints. Omit `per_page` and these endpoints return 25 records. The maximum is 500; a larger value returns `400 Bad Request`. A blank, zero, negative, or non-numeric value is not rejected — it sets the page size to 100, not to 25.

Locale.name: locale
Locale.description:
Override the response locale. Affects localized fields such as core
role names. Resolution order: this param > subdomain > org default >
app default (en).

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description:
ETag from a previous GET response. When present, the server checks
that the resource has not been modified since your read. If the ETag
is stale, a 409 Conflict is returned. Omit this header for
unconditional (last-write-wins) updates.

Q.name: q
Q.description:
Full-text search filter. Matches against the resource's searchable text
fields using Postgres full-text search (`simple` + `unaccent`). Supports
Google-style syntax: `marketing -intern`, `"exact phrase"`, `foo OR bar`.
Composes with other filters (all AND'd together). Empty or whitespace-only
values are ignored. Malformed queries return no rows rather than an error.

ActorIdFilter.name: actor_id
ActorIdFilter.description: Only items whose `actor_id` is this person (`per_`) or agent (`agt_`). Splits the items of a role filled by several people. An unknown, invisible, or malformed id returns an empty list, not an error.

IncludeLegacyId.name: include_legacy_id
IncludeLegacyId.description:
**Transition-only.** When `true`, each resource in the response
additionally carries a `legacy_id` field — its v3 sequential integer id
— so v3-keyed integrators can correlate v5 TypeIDs with the numeric IDs
they already hold during migration. Default is off (`legacy_id` is
omitted unless explicitly requested).

This is a temporary v3→v5 bridge and **NOT a permanent part of the v5
contract**: it retires when the v3 API retires. See the "Legacy IDs
(transition-only)" section in the API overview. Applies to the standard
resource list/show endpoints and `/me`; nested `?include=` embeds are
out of scope.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `?cursor=` to fetch the next page. Present when `has_next_page` is true, except on feeds documented as resumable (`GET /me/messages`), where it is present whenever there is a position to resume from.

description.description: For structural (constitutional) accountabilities, resolved from the Holacracy Constitution in the request locale. For custom accountabilities, the org-defined description.
description.example: Defining coding standards for the team

is_structural.description: True for constitutional accountabilities defined by the Holacracy Constitution (e.g., Facilitator's meeting facilitation duties). False for org-defined custom accountabilities.

is_inherited.description: True when this accountability is inherited from another role (e.g., a sub-circle Lead Link inheriting from the anchor Lead Link). False for accountabilities defined directly on this role.

description.description: For structural (constitutional) domains, resolved from the Holacracy Constitution in the request locale. For custom domains, the org-defined description.

is_structural.description: True for constitutional domains defined by the Holacracy Constitution. False for org-defined custom domains.

is_inherited.description: True when this domain is inherited from another role (e.g., a sub-circle Lead Link inheriting from the anchor Lead Link). False for domains defined directly on this role.

legacy_id.description: **Transition-only.** The role's v3 sequential integer id, present ONLY when `?include_legacy_id=true` is passed. A v3→v5 migration bridge for correlating TypeIDs with the numeric IDs integrators already hold; NOT a permanent part of the v5 contract — this field retires when the v3 API retires. See the "Legacy IDs" section in the API overview.

name.description:
Localized display name. For core roles, applies the organization's
custom term overrides first, then locale-based translation (via
`?locale=` param, subdomain, or org default). Custom roles pass
through unchanged.

short_name.description:
User-set display-name override for circle-roles (roles where
`has_subroles` is true). Null for non-circle roles and for
circle-roles with no override set. Useful for building compact
handles or labels from the shorter name people actually use.

purpose.example: Steering the role toward its purpose

parent_role_id.description: ID of the parent role. Null for anchor roles.

original_role_id.description:
ID of the role this role derives from — its original role.
Non-null on linked roles (which surface `linked` in `flags`) and
focus roles; `null` for all other roles. A cross-linked role
appears as two v5 records with different `id`s; the linked record
points here at its original, letting a consumer correlate the two.

has_subroles.description: Whether this role is expanded with subroles.

flags.description:
Classification flags. `structural` = core Holacracy role,
`elected` = filled by election, `linked` = cross-linked from another role.

fillers.description: People and agents currently filling this role.

tags.description: Tag names applied to this role.

RoleDetail.description: A role with optional included resources (detail view).

parent_role.description: Present when `?include=parent_role` is requested. Null for anchor roles.

skills.description: Present when `?include=skills` is requested. Returns skill summaries (no `content`); fetch full content on demand via `GET /skills/{id}`.

TreeNode.description:
A role in the tree response. `children` is always present (possibly
empty). `accountabilities`, `domains`, `fillers`, and `assignments`
are present only when their corresponding `?include=` value is set.

short_name.description:
User-set display-name override for circle-roles. Null for
non-circle roles and for circle-roles with no override set.

parent_role_id.description:
ID of the parent role. Null for the anchor role. Present on every
node even though nesting is already conveyed by `children`, so
that consumers who flatten the tree to a list retain the edge.

original_role_id.description:
ID of the role this node derives from — its original role.
Non-null on linked roles (which surface `linked` in `flags`) and
focus roles; `null` for all other roles.

children.description:
Direct children of this node, each of which is itself a
`TreeNode`. Empty array when the node is a leaf, when `?depth`
truncates beneath it, or when all children are hidden by
authorization.

Assignment.description:
A role assignment. `role_id` and `actor_id` are always present.
Use `?include=actor` or `?include=role` to embed the full related object.

role_id.description: The role being filled. Always present.

actor_id.description: The person or agent filling the role. Always present.

focus.description: Optional focus area for the assignment.

id.description: The person or agent API ID.

email.description: The actor's email address. Present for human actors; null for agents.

AgentSession.description:
A record of an agent session, exactly as GlassFrog stored it.

The fields are a projection of what the start/end lifecycle calls
wrote — no liveness is computed on read. `status` is therefore the
organization's *belief* about the session, which is precisely what
makes it useful for reconciliation against host truth.

agent_id.description: The agent this session belongs to.

role_id.description: The role the session was started for. Null for an agent-level session that is not scoped to any role.

assignment_id.description: The assignment backing a role session, when there is one.

topic.description: Topic scoping the session, typically a ticket id. Null for a primary session. Several topic sessions may share one role.

identifier.description: Client-supplied identifier for the session (for example a tmux session name). Free text, set by the caller at start and never server-generated, so it is only as meaningful and as unique as the caller made it. Filter on it to recover your own record.

status.description: The stored lifecycle state. `active` means no end call was recorded — not that the session is verified running.

summary.description: What the session accomplished. Written when it ends.

ended_at.description: When the session was recorded as ended. Null while active.

last_seen_at.description: Last heartbeat timestamp. Stamped by the heartbeat endpoint; sessions that predate the feature carry a backfilled value. Null for ended sessions that were never heartbeated.

heartbeat_interval.description: Client-declared heartbeat interval in seconds. Used to derive the stale threshold (3× interval). Null uses the server default (60 seconds).

liveness_state.description: Derived on read from last_seen_at and heartbeat_interval. fresh = within 3× interval; stale = past 3× interval but not yet expired; ended = session is ended; unknown = no heartbeat data.

ended_reason.description: Why the session ended. Set by endSession or the expiry job. Null for active sessions or ended sessions that predate this field.

Target.description:
A target (key result) under a goal. Progress is computed on read via

`ending_value == starting_value` → 100 if current ≥ ending else 0.

role_id.description:
The role the target is assigned to. May differ from the parent
goal's role (cross-circle target alignment is supported).

current_value.description:
The value from the latest kept progress update on this target.
Null when the target has no progress updates yet.

ProposalChange.description:
A governance change command within a proposal. Shape varies by `type`,
which serves as the discriminator.

**Top-level types** — valid as direct children of a proposal's
`changes` array: `CreateRole`, `UpdateRole`, `RemoveRole`,
`CreatePolicy`, `UpdatePolicy`, `RemovePolicy`, `CreateLinkedRole`,
`UpdateLinkedRole`, `MoveRole`, `MovePolicy`, `MoveItems`,
`ElectRoleFiller`.

**Nested-only types** — must appear within the `children` array of a
role-level change (`CreateRole`, `UpdateRole`, or
`UpdateLinkedRole`), not as top-level proposal changes:
`CreateAccountability`, `UpdateAccountability`,
`RemoveAccountability`, `CreateDomain`, `UpdateDomain`,
`RemoveDomain`. The server rejects nested-only types at the top level
with a 422 error naming the valid parent types.

**Read-only types** — appear on older proposals but are not accepted
on input: `CreateRoleNote`, `UpdateRoleNote`, `RemoveRoleNote`,
`UpdateTags`. They carry only `id`, `type` and (role notes)
`target_id`.

On input, the `type` field also accepts `snake_case` and aliases
(e.g. `remove_role`, `DeleteRole` → `RemoveRole`). Responses always
use the canonical PascalCase names shown in the discriminator.

**Identifier fields** use `snake_case` with `_id` suffix and carry
TypeID values (e.g. `role_id: "role_abc..."`, `target_id: "pol_abc..."`).
The `target_id` field identifies the entity being created, updated,
or removed — its TypeID prefix indicates the entity type.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 Problem Details error object (backward-compatible successor to RFC 7807). All 4xx and 5xx responses from the API use this shape. Additional members may be present as RFC 9457 "extensions".

limit_config_key.description: Extension member. Present on a 422 that rejects content for being too large. Names the server configuration key that produced `max_content_length`, so a limit that looks wrong can be traced to the setting that set it.

reason.description: Extension member. Machine-readable denial reason, present on 403 responses raised by skill authorization rules so a denied caller can tell which rule applied. `ai_integration_disabled` — the organization's AI-integration flag is off. `ownership_required` — the caller is not a linked owner of the skill (ownership derives from kept skill links). `sole_ownership_required` — the skill is co-owned (2+ kept links); delete requires sole ownership. `self_link_only` — link and unlink targets may only be the caller's own agent, or a role the caller fills.

ContentSizeWarnings.description: Warnings about the saved record. Present only when there is something to report.
